intro.title: What Is an Online Complaint Management System?
paragraphs: An online complaint management system is a web-based portal where customers register complaints and your team tracks each one until it is resolved. Instead of complaints getting lost in email inboxes, phone notes and spreadsheets, every issue gets a complaint number, an owner, a deadline and a full history that customers and managers can check at any time.

Our complaint management software gives each person exactly what they need. Customers log a complaint and check its status. Admins see every complaint on a dashboard, add service engineers and agents, and assign work. Service engineers log in, view the complaints assigned to them, resolve them and update the status, often from a mobile app in the field. Automatic emails, SMS and escalations keep everything moving.

Handling complaints well saves time and money, builds customer loyalty and shows you exactly which products or processes need fixing. We customise the system around your categories, teams and service levels, and connect it to your <crm>CRM</crm> and other tools. <contact>Tell us how you handle complaints today</contact>.

offerings.title: Features of Our Complaint Management Software

process.title: How the Complaint Management Workflow Works
process.subtitle: From the moment a customer reports a problem to the moment they confirm it is fixed, every step is tracked.

steps.title: Customer logs a complaint
steps.desc: Through the web portal, app, phone, email or WhatsApp, with details and photos.

steps.title: Automatic confirmation
steps.desc: The complaint is saved in the central database and the customer receives a complaint number by email or SMS.

steps.title: Admin reviews and assigns
steps.desc: The administrator reviews the complaint, or rules assign it automatically, to the right service engineer or agent.

steps.title: Engineer resolves the issue
steps.desc: The service engineer acts on the complaint, updates the status and records what was done.

steps.title: Escalation if needed
steps.desc: If the SLA is at risk, the complaint escalates automatically to supervisors so nothing is ignored.

steps.title: Customer updated and closed
steps.desc: The customer is informed of the resolution, confirms closure and can rate the service. The full history is kept.

tech.title: What Each User Can Do
tech.subtitle: Separate logins and permissions for every role keep the process clear and secure.

faqs.title: Online Complaint Management System FAQs
faqs.subtitle: Quick answers about complaint management software.

items.q: What is an online complaint management system?
items.a: An online complaint management system is a web-based portal that helps businesses record, assign, track and resolve customer complaints. Customers log complaints and check their status, admins assign them, and service engineers resolve them and update progress.

items.q: Why is a complaint management system important?
items.a: It makes sure no complaint is lost, every issue has an owner and a deadline, and customers are kept informed. That leads to faster resolutions, more loyal customers and data that shows which problems to fix at the root.

items.q: Is there a free complaint management system?
items.a: Free and open-source complaint tools exist and can work for very small volumes. Most growing businesses outgrow them because of limited workflows, mobile apps, integrations and support. A custom system fits your process and you own it, with no monthly per-user fees.

items.q: How much time does it take to develop a complaint management system?
items.a: An essential complaint management system usually takes 3 to 6 weeks. Adding an engineer mobile app, SLAs and WhatsApp takes 1 to 3 months, and enterprise systems take 3 months or more.

items.q: How much does it cost to develop a complaint management system?
items.a: Typical costs are $3,000 to $8,000 for an essential system, $8,000 to $20,000 for an advanced system with a mobile app, and $20,000 or more for enterprise needs. We give a fixed quote after a free consultation.

items.q: Is there a mobile app, and can it connect to our CRM?
items.a: Yes. Service engineers get an Android and iOS app, customers can use a mobile-friendly portal or app, and the system can integrate with your CRM, ERP, email, SMS and WhatsApp.
